// purpose: Lumen Supply, the Next.js 16 App Router app this repository instruments. It imports no workspace package, so it declares no project `references`.
// format: Strict JSON, so notes are top-level `"// …"` keys, which TypeScript ignores and Next.js neither requires nor suggests; inside `compilerOptions` such a key is an error (TS5023).
// next-rewrite: `next dev` and `next build` rewrite tsconfig.json through writeConfigurationDefaults() unless the raw file contains `extends` or `references`. The `extends` below keeps this file byte-stable: a rewrite would dirty `git status` and fail the `residual-worktree` rule of `pnpm check:no-residual-instrumentation`. Every compiler option Next.js requires or suggests is also present in the raw file: required ones with Next's values, suggested ones as well, where `target`, `lib`, `allowJs`, `strict` and `noEmit` deliberately differ from the suggestion. Next leaves those alone because it writes a suggestion only when the key is missing.
// compilerOptions.emit: `noEmit` is false where Next.js suggests true: a composite project with emit disabled writes only its .tsbuildinfo and contributes nothing to the solution build. `tsc -b` emits declarations only, into .tsbuild; `next build` produces the app.
// compilerOptions.lib: DOM and DOM.Iterable join ES2023 for the client components.
// compilerOptions.verbatimModuleSyntax: Stated together with `isolatedModules`: Next.js requires `isolatedModules` unless the raw file sets `verbatimModuleSyntax`, so both branches of its check match.
// compilerOptions.jsx: Next.js 16 requires "react-jsx", the React automatic runtime.
// compilerOptions.strict: `strict`, `strictNullChecks` and `allowJs: false` are stated against Next.js's suggested `strict: false` and `allowJs: true`.
// compilerOptions.skipLibCheck: Does not cover the generated Prisma client under src/generated/prisma: it is TypeScript source and is checked as first-party code.
// compilerOptions.plugins: The Next.js language-service plugin, for editors; tsc ignores it.
// compilerOptions.types: node, react and react-dom are named because TypeScript 6.0 includes no @types package that `types` omits.
// compilerOptions.paths: The single alias `@/*` -> ./src/*. `baseUrl` is absent: TypeScript 6.0.3 rejects it (TS5101), and both tsc and Next.js resolve `paths` without it.
// include: next-env.d.ts is generated and git-ignored, so it sits in `include`, where a missing match is ignored, rather than in `files`, where it is an error; nothing may depend on it, which is why the app uses no static image imports. Both .next/types and .next/dev/types globs are listed so Next.js never appends one.
// exclude: `exclude` replaces the base list, so .tsbuild is repeated. .next is not excluded, because the `include` globs pick up its generated route types.
